subject: HealthSync — SDK/Auth & Routing: post-demo architecture checklist
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-06-21T15:12:00Z
Subject: HealthSync — post-demo: SDK/auth & routing follow-ups

Hi Ellen — thanks for the time today, really appreciate the walk-through of the ingestion pipeline and the patient-safety review. Per our demo, I wanted to capture the key integration points and next steps for your engineering team so we can scope the dedicated deployment and early routing policy work.

Quick summary / action items from my side:
- SDK onboarding: HealthSync will evaluate the JS + Python SDKs for initial PoC (web UI ingestion + backend enrichment).
- Auth model: Rajiv flagged wanting token rotation + KMS-backed keys (we discussed API keys vs short-lived JWTs).
- Routing & fallbacks: requirement to route sensitive PHI workloads to our dedicated VPC deployment in us-east-1, default to hosted for non-PHI; low-latency paths for triage flows (p95 < 250ms).
- Structured output / tool calling: you want JSON-schema enforcement and the ability to trigger an internal clinical decision tool via tool-calling.
- Embeddings / rerankers: initial plan to use embeddings for semantic search and a reranker on top for recall precision.

Next steps I promise to deliver this week: a concise integration checklist (SDK install snippets + example auth flows), a proposed model routing policy draft, and a small sample of recommended structured-output schemas. Attaching an implementation requirements PDF and a short SDK setup guide for your engineers.

Attachments: [healthsync-implementation-requirements.pdf (application/pdf)], [redwood-sdk-setup.md (text/markdown)]

If that looks right, can you confirm the two engineering contacts who should receive the setup docs? Also, Rajiv — can you confirm whether HealthSync will require customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own key) or if Redwood-managed KMS is acceptable for the PoC?

Thanks — Aisha

Thanks Aisha — great demo. Confirming the two contacts: Ellen (frontend lead) and me (platform/security lead). A few clarifications from our side before we start the SDK eval: 

1) Auth & keys: For the initial PoC we prefer Redwood-managed KMS, however we'll need the option to switch to customer-managed keys before production. Can you outline the steps and downtime (if any) for key rotation / ownership transfer?

2) Network / VPC: Any docs on VPC peering vs private-link style connectivity for the dedicated deployment? We need a sketch of required routes and a list of open ports.

3) Data residency / routing: We need firm guarantees on routing policy — e.g., "PHI flows must never be served by hosted shared instances" and an option to pin model variants to dedicated nodes. How do you implement and enforce that at the routing layer?

4) Embeddings & reranker: For our semantic search use case, do you recommend using your hosted embedding model first or bringing our own model artifact? What are the tradeoffs on latency/cost and how would fallback chains work if our primary reranker is unavailable?

Appreciate a short tech note addressing these points. Happy to loop in procurement later for EULA/pricing once we validate the architecture.

-Rajiv

Thanks — I've drafted the tech note below. Ben, feel free to edit the routing/embedding parts before we send. I'm keeping it tight for Rajiv's review.

--- BEGIN TECH NOTE (engineer-friendly) ---
Purpose: Answer HealthSync's Qs on auth/KMS, network, routing enforcement, and embeddings fallback behavior.

1) Auth & KMS
- PoC: Redwood-managed KMS is supported immediately. For production we support BYOK via customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS/Supplied HSM).
- Key rotation & ownership transfer: we use envelope encryption. Steps: (1) create CMK in customer's account and provide a key policy binding to Redwood service principal; (2) configure Redwood Private to use the CMK ARN; (3) perform validation (test decrypt) — zero downtime for data encrypted with envelope keys; actual re-encrypt of stored artifacts is background and transparent.
- Short-lived tokens: recommended pattern is short JWTs (15m) with refresh via a rotating service token; SDKs include automatic refresh helpers (see attached redwood-sdk-setup.md snippet).

2) Network connectivity
- Options: VPC peering (simpler to set up, cross-account IAM/route table adjustments) vs PrivateLink (higher security, managed endpoint service). PrivateLink is recommended for regulated PHI workloads because it avoids routing across public IPs.
- Ports: allow outbound 443 to Redwood control plane; for PrivateLink there are no open inbound public ports. For dedicated pools we require an egress rule to our IP ranges (documented in the attached PDF).

3) Routing & enforcement
- Enforcement model: routing is policy-driven and evaluated at the front proxy layer before a request is assigned to a pool. Policies are declarative JSON objects attached to the customer config. Example snippet: 

  {"match": {"sensitivity":"phi"}, "route": {"deployment":"dedicated-us-east-1", "pin": true}}

- PHI guarantee: requests labeled as sensitivity=phi are only routed to dedicated pools; the control plane rejects any policy that would route PHI to shared-hosted pools. Audit logs record routing decisions and are available via the console/Log API.
- Latency policies: configurable SLOs (p95 threshold). If p95 > threshold for 3 consecutive windows, the evaluator can: (a) route to a higher-tier pool, (b) fall back to a quantized model variant, or (c) switch to a different region (if allowed).

4) Fallback chain example
- Primary: full-precision model (redwood-xl-13b) pinned to dedicated nodes
- Fallback-1: quantized variant (redwood-xl-13b-q4) on dedicated nodes — lower cost and smaller memory footprint
- Fallback-2: smaller low-latency model (redwood-mini-3b-hosted) in hosted region for non-PHI only

Routing evaluator pseudocode: 
- if request.sensitivity == 'phi' -> enforce dedicated-only chain
- else evaluate latency/cost policy: if expected_token_cost > budget -> select cached/quantized variant
- monitor real-time p95; on breach, escalate to next fallback and emit an incident metric

5) Embeddings & reranker guidance
- Hosted embeddings: fastest to get started, good throughput and automatic scaling. Tradeoff: you give inference calls to hosted service (no private model unless you bring one).
- Bring-your-own model (BYOM): supports lower-latency local inference and control over vector format; requires packaging the model with recommended tokenizer and quantization profile.
- Recommendation: start hosted for PoC to validate vector semantics, then migrate to BYOM for production if residency or cost becomes a priority.
- Reranker fallback: the reranker sits after candidate retrieval. If primary reranker fails or is overloaded, the system can: (a) use a heuristic scoring function, (b) fall back to an earlier production reranker, or (c) serve un-reranked candidates with a feature flag. We recommend a simple published fallback chain and a canary rollout of reranker changes.

6) SDK & code snippets (high-level)
- JS install: npm install --save @redwood/inference
- Example auth - short token with refresh:

  const client = new RedwoodClient({authProvider: rotateTokenProvider()});
  await client.generate({model: 'redwood-xl-13b', input: ...});

- Example routing policy (JSON):

  {"policy_name": "healthsync-phi-enforce","rules": [{"match":{"sensitivity":"phi"},"route":{"deployment":"dedicated-us-east-1","pin":true}}]}

7) Next steps & deliverables
- We will send a polished one-page tech note (this doc) + an example routing policy file + a network connectivity checklist for the HealthSync infra team.
- Proposed timeline: engineering Q&A by Thu, PoC SDK install by next Wed, policy review & canary the following week.

--- END TECH NOTE ---

Ben — routing + embeddings section needs your approval/edits; once we align I'll send to Rajiv and Ellen with attachments.

- Dev
